items.title: Jack Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 24, 1997
items.q: Fat Jenkins I remember was the trumpet player. Isn’t this funny — that many years ago and I remember his name? Wow.

ctx.x: You were rehearsing with the acts that came in, you had to provide different kinds of music for whether it was a dance routine or a comedic —.

Whatever music they had. They had their own charts, and if they didn’t have a chart of something they wanted, they’d say, “I’m used to playing ‘Tea for Two’” for instance, and I’d do a chorus and a half of this or whatever, whatever. I sing a chorus and dance a chorus and then whatever. And so we’d rehearse and then we’d do the show at night. And I was pretty well liked I guess, it seemed anyway, because I was doing pretty good at it, and the acts — word got around in New York. They got a good band over in…
Well those acts probably appreciated when they could come in and give you the music.
